title: Verdict and Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of Harlan Voss, founder of the river town of Calloway's Bend, is exhumed for a land dispute, insurance investigator Ansel Zhou discovers it empty — and her photographic memory of a thirty-year-old claim file becomes the only evidence anyone has. As she reconstructs the night Voss supposedly died, every alibi in town begins to crack, and someone starts killing the witnesses to keep the past buried. Ansel must choose between protecting the one person who saved her life and exposing a murder the whole town conspired to forget; in the end, she testifies, the living murderer is arrested, and Voss himself — alive, old, and unrepentant — walks into the river he once faked his death beside.
about_author: Lior Pemberton is a former claims adjuster from the Ohio Valley who spent a decade reading other people's disasters before writing them. Verdict and Autopsy is their third novel and first mystery.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty
chapters.summary: Ansel Zhou attends the court-ordered exhumation of Harlan Voss as the insurer's representative. When the casket lid opens on nothing but river stones, her photographic memory flashes back to the 1994 death certificate. POV: Ansel. Beat: cold professional curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Rain
chapters.summary: Ansel pulls the original policy file and finds her own mentor, Ruth Okafor, signed off on the payout. Ruth warns her off with unusual fear. POV: Ansel. Beat: the first hint that the case was buried deliberately, not sloppily.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Voss's daughter Camille hires Ansel privately — she never believed her father drowned. Their interview reveals Harlan had enemies over the mill land. POV: Ansel. Beat: reluctant alliance formed over shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Alibi in Amber
chapters.summary: Ansel interviews Dale Pruitt, the sheriff who closed the drowning case, now dying of emphysema. His alibi for the night Voss vanished is word-for-word identical to three other witnesses' statements. POV: Ansel. Beat: the uncanny recognition that memory itself has been manufactured.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel dives the old mill sluice where the body should have been found and recovers a belt buckle stamped with mill property marks. Someone watches from the bank. POV: Ansel. Beat: triumph shadowed by the realization she's being tracked.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: A chapter from 1994, following young mill foreman Teddy Brandt on the night of the disappearance — he drove a drugged man to the river and was paid in cash by someone whose face he never saw. POV: Teddy (past). Beat: complicity and terror.

chapters.title: Small Town Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ansel maps the five alibis against payroll records and finds all five were on Voss's private payroll the month after the payout. The conspiracy had a budget. POV: Ansel. Beat: intellectual exhilaration turning to isolation.

chapters.title: Ruth's Silence
chapters.summary: Ansel confronts Ruth, who admits she suspected fraud but was threatened — and that the threat came from inside the insurance company itself. POV: Ruth. Beat: betrayal; loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: The First Witness Falls
chapters.summary: Dale Pruitt dies in a house fire ruled accidental, hours before a scheduled second interview. Ansel recognizes the accelerant pattern from a claim she processed years ago. POV: Ansel. Beat: grief and guilt — her questions killed him.

chapters.title: Camille's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Camille confesses she hired Ansel not for truth but to stall the land dispute long enough to sell the mill property. Ansel feels used but understands survival. POV: Ansel. Beat: disillusionment; everyone has a price.

chapters.title: Teddy Now
chapters.summary: Present-day Teddy Brandt, a respected funeral director, receives an envelope of old cash and a photograph of his daughter. He burns the note and prepares to lie again. POV: Teddy. Beat: the price of survival, thirty years compounded with interest.

chapters.title: The Face Behind the Money
chapters.summary: Ansel traces the payroll disbursements to a shell company and finds the signature of Marcus Hale — the town's current mayor and Voss's former accountant. POV: Ansel. Beat: the conspiracy has a living head, and he runs the town.

chapters.title: Offered a Coffin
chapters.summary: Hale offers Ansel a lucrative consulting contract and hints at her own buried past — the identity she fled before coming to Calloway's Bend. POV: Ansel. Beat: temptation weaponized through identity; her theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Ansel matches a 1994 photo of the marina to the alibi statements and spots a sixth figure no statement mentions: a woman in a red coat. Ruth wore red the week Voss died. POV: Ansel. Beat: devastating suspicion aimed at the person who raised her professionally.

chapters.title: Confession at the Sluice
chapters.summary: Ruth admits she helped plan the fake death — Voss wanted out of his debts and his life — but swears she never knew a real body would be needed. Someone else did die that night. POV: Ruth. Beat: the mystery deepens; the empty coffin hides a corpse after all.

chapters.title: The Second Witness
chapters.summary: Teddy Brandt disappears; his funeral home is found scrubbed with bleach. Ansel realizes the killer is erasing the chain of hands, working backward toward whoever gave the order. POV: Ansel. Beat: escalating dread; the clock is audible now.

chapters.title: What Ansel Buried
chapters.summary: Hale leaks Ansel's former identity to the town — she once testified against her own family and changed her name. Her credibility collapses publicly just before she can act. POV: Ansel. Beat: rock bottom; identity as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The Night of the Flood
chapters.summary: A full reconstruction chapter: 1994, the drugged man in Teddy's trunk was not Voss but Voss's blackmailer, mill clerk Owen Reyes — murdered so the fake death could hold. Voss watched from the bank. POV: multiple (past). Beat: horror revealed; the beloved founder was a killer.

chapters.title: Harlan Voss, Living
chapters.summary: Following the money to a lakeside cabin, Ansel finds Voss alive under another name, unrepentant, arguing that Owen Reyes deserved it. She records his confession on her phone. POV: Ansel. Beat: the climax of discovery — truth captured, safety nowhere near guaranteed.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Hale's men corner Ansel at the cabin; Voss, valuing his freedom over allies, helps subdue them to keep his confession from becoming hers alone. State police arrive with the recording already uploaded. POV: Ansel. Beat: violent climax resolved by wit and the memory she was mocked for.

chapters.title: Autopsy
chapters.summary: Owen Reyes is finally exhumed from the mill foundation and returned to his family; Hale is indicted, Ruth takes a plea, and Camille sells the land to fund Reyes's memorial. Ansel testifies under her real name, reclaiming it. POV: Ansel. Beat: justice incomplete but real; identity chosen, not hidden.

chapters.title: The River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Months later, Ansel visits the sluice where it began. A fisherman mentions an old man who walked into the river at dawn and was never found. She files no report. POV: Ansel. Beat: quiet resolution — some verdicts belong to the water.
